model.notes: Take rules target the cluster of rejected pump-fade shorts (mostly JCT, MAGMA, EVAA, ARIA) where momentum had already stalled; both exclude still-accelerating pumps, which existing skip rules handle. Skip rules extend the momentum-vs-floor-distance logic to high-leverage shorts with a hot last hour regardless of the 4h move (e.g. PARTI, LSK, APR) and to crowded-short cases at 10x+.

accepted_now: Skip 20x+ shorts on names whose last 4h is up 5% or more.
Skip shorts at 10x or more while the 4h move is at least +10% and the last hour is still not falling.
Skip 20x+ shorts while the last hour is still up 2.5% or more, whatever the 4h move.

new.why: Price has already squeezed up 2.5%+ since the signal, but buyers are now a minority of the tape. The burst of buying is exhausting, so we short from a higher level after the adverse leg. The remaining adverse excursion should be small enough for a 3% stop.
Price rises while open interest falls: shorts are covering, not new longs entering. Once the squeeze fuel is spent, an entry right after it is less likely to see another leg against us.

Retail is crowded long, trading activity is quiet (no fresh buying burst) and price sits at or above the signal level. Longs are trapped without momentum, which favours a straight-for path with low adverse excursion that suits a 2% stop.
Positive funding after a 4-hour pump means longs are paying to hold. Wait until BTC stops rising in the hour, so there is no market tailwind for a continued squeeze.

patterns.notes: Entry rules target post-squeeze states: price already up since the signal while open interest unwinds or buying fades.
